content: Nizatidine is a medication prescribed to treat and prevent the recurrence of ulcers. It is also used to manage conditions where the stomach produces excessive acid. Additionally, it can be used to treat or prevent occasional heartburn, acid indigestion, or sour stomach. This medication works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Nizatidine is available both as a prescription and over-the-counter medication. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Nizatidine is available in tablet and capsule forms, which are taken orally. It is typically taken once daily at bedtime or twice a day, with or without food. Follow the instructions provided on the package or your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take nizatidine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of the medication or take it more frequently than prescribed. If symptoms of heartburn, acid indigestion, or sour stomach persist for more than two weeks while using nizatidine, discontinue use and contact your doctor. Before taking nizatidine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to nizatidine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, including aspirin, antacids (such as Maalox or Mylanta), and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking nizatidine, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose of nizatidine, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Nizatidine may cause mild side effects. Notify your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: Headache Dizziness Drowsiness Constipation Diarrhea Stomach pain Runny nose Sneezing Coughing Sweating In rare cases, nizatidine may cause severe side effects. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: Skin rash Hives Itching Wheezing Difficulty breathing If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store nizatidine in the original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor while taking nizatidine. Do not share this medication with others. If you have any questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Nizatidine is sold under the following brand names: Axid® Axid® AR Acid Reducer Axid® Pulvules®
